analysis.title: Weekly Pulse: Rebalancing US Equities
key_insights: Risk assets lacked direction in the week to 23 Oct 2026 while oil gyrated on supply concerns. Gold extended its slide with real yields elevated.
Equity ETF flows went mainly to global and EM exposures. Fixed income saw renewed flows into euro and USD government debt.

US equity UCITS ETFs have gathered close to EUR 30bn net new assets since June versus EUR 11.6bn for Europe equity UCITS ETFs. 76% of flows went to broad US large cap exposures, but the pace of asset gathering has slowed since July.
Amundi names higher rates, rising energy prices and AI/tech underperformance despite resilient earnings as factors that may have moderated demand for US equities.

S&P 500 EPS upgrades are concentrated in three sectors, with most of the index revised at or below the index average. Amundi stays selective on US equities and prefers exposures beyond highly valued mega caps.

CFTC data shows asset managers' net positions in S&P 500 e-mini futures have recovered since March and remain well above the long-term average, a broadly constructive stance despite weaker performance since the summer.

Midterm elections: Amundi's base case is a divided Congress, while market predictions increasingly favour a Democrat sweep. Since 1946 the S&P 500 averages +1.2% in the three months before midterms (50% hit rate) and +7.9% in the three months after.
A split Congress has historically been the weakest post-election configuration, averaging +2.1% over three months versus +9.1% for a more evenly split Republican/Democrat outcome.

With tariffs and geopolitics already central to the administration's agenda, a divided legislature is likely to reinforce existing policy priorities and sustain uncertainty the market must price after the election.
Since 31 March 2026 returns in MSCI USA have been dominated by semiconductor, AI infrastructure and cybersecurity names. That concentration has begun to reverse in October.
Of 513 MSCI USA constituents, 70% have a positive return month to date, yet MSCI USA is -0.1%, because the AI and semiconductor selloff is hitting the largest weights.
Month to date in October, MSCI USA ex Mega Cap is +3.1% versus -0.1% for MSCI USA. The ex-mega-cap index trades at 17.5x forward P/E versus 18.8x for MSCI USA.
Information Technology is 37.3% of MSCI USA. The ex-mega-cap variant tilts toward Financials (11.9%), Health Care (10.0%) and Industrials (8.2%).

Amundi suggests considering a 50/50 blend of MSCI USA and MSCI USA ex Mega Caps for a more resilient profile. On index data to 30 Sep, the blend had 1Y volatility of 9.7 and Sharpe of 1.65, versus 12.6 and 1.51 for MSCI USA.

sector_views.sector: US mega cap technology / AI and semiconductors
sector_views.rationale: Amundi calls for a blended allocation because concentrated AI and semiconductor leadership is reversing sharply.
The ex-mega-cap index is +3.1% month to date and trades at a forward P/E discount to MSCI USA.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 EPS upgrades have been heavily concentrated in three sectors, with most of the index revised at or below the index average.
AI/tech stocks have underperformed despite resilient earnings, per Amundi.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed decision is expected to dominate the week. Guidance on the path ahead is the key focus given elevated rates.
The ECB decision is expected to dominate the week alongside the Fed, with guidance the focus.

trade_ideas.description: Blend 50% MSCI USA with 50% MSCI USA ex Mega Caps (index exposure via Amundi ETFs, no US-listed ticker named)
trade_ideas.rationale: Reduces vulnerability to concentrated AI and semiconductor reversals while keeping mega-cap growth exposure.

risk_factors: Narrow market leadership in AI and semiconductor names, where a reversal can drag index-level returns.
Higher rates and rising energy prices.
Midterm election volatility and a divided Congress sustaining policy uncertainty.
Sustainability of large US technology capital expenditure plans.
Supply chain disruption concerns for the software industry.
charts_described: Asset managers' net position in S&P 500 e-mini futures (CFTC) has recovered since March and sits above the long-term average.
S&P 500 performance since 1946 shows a 3-month pre-election average of +1.2% and a 3-month post-election average of +7.9%, with a split Congress weakest post-election at +2.1%.
vol_and_positioning: Near-term volatility is the norm ahead of US midterm elections, with subdued pre-election returns averaging +1.2% and a 50% hit rate across 20 cycles since 1946.
Asset managers' net S&P 500 e-mini futures positions have recovered since March and sit well above the long-term average.
Market concentration is high: a reversal in a handful of AI and semiconductor names is dragging index-level returns even as 70% of constituents are positive.
geopolitical: US midterm elections approaching, with markets increasingly favouring a Democrat sweep and Amundi's base case a divided Congress.
Tariffs and geopolitical positioning are central to the Trump administration's agenda.
China's Plenum could provide some fiscal stimulus signals.
Oil price swings on supply concerns.
